quotes.text: Co-pilot is a helpful colleague beside you. An agent is a trained team member with a narrow job, a written rule book, and a manager checking the results.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a crisp, memorable line between an assistant and an agent.

quotes.text: Notice the word approved. An agent doesn't get free access to everything. People decide what it can read, what it can change, and when it must stop and ask for help.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core control principle behind Dynamics 365 agents.

quotes.text: An agent should never guess its way through a situation where the wrong answer costs money, harms a relationship, or creates a promise your company cannot keep.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear rule for when an agent must hand work to a person.

quotes.text: An agent should only reach the records and actions needed for its specific job. A sales agent doesn't need permission to change finance records, and a supplier agent doesn't need access to every customer case.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete least-privilege advice for agent access.

quotes.text: Don't start with the messiest process in the company. Instead, start with a queue where people already agree on what good work looks like.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical recommendation for choosing a first agent use case.

chapters.title: Finance, operations and supply chain agents
What to put in place first

takeaways: Dynamics 365 agents work from triggers in the background, unlike Copilot, which responds when you ask it something.
Every agent needs approved data, written rules, guardrails and clear hand-over points where a person reviews risky actions.
Start with one repeated, measurable job and clean data, test with real examples and only then expand.
hook: Leads pile up, cases wait and supplier emails go unanswered when nobody asks Copilot for help. This episode explains for business and IT teams what Dynamics 365 agents do across sales, service, finance and supply chain. You will learn how they work behind the scenes and where people stay in control.
